title: 4SD0 chemistry practicals: methods summary
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
unit: Spring 1: Revision cycle 1: Biology 1 to 2, Chemistry 1 to 2, Physics 1 to 4
source: Written for gcse-science/y11 lesson 103 (Practical methods summary sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Key steps for the chemistry practicals revised in lesson 103. Learn the method, the measurements and one safety point for each.

panels.title: Empirical formula of magnesium oxide
points: Weigh a crucible and lid; add magnesium ribbon and weigh again.
Heat strongly, lifting the lid now and then to let oxygen in.
Heat to constant mass; cool and weigh.
Mass of oxygen = final mass − magnesium mass; divide each mass by Ar and find the simplest ratio (MgO).

panels.title: Making a soluble salt (e.g. copper sulfate)
points: Warm dilute sulfuric acid; add excess copper oxide until no more dissolves.
Filter off the excess solid.
Heat the filtrate to the point of crystallisation; leave to cool and crystallise.
Dry the crystals on filter paper.

panels.title: Rates of reaction
points: Change one variable (temperature, concentration, surface area).
Measure gas volume with a gas syringe, or mass loss on a balance, at regular times.
Keep other variables the same.
Plot a graph; the steeper the gradient, the faster the rate.

panels.title: Tests for ions and gases
points: Hydrogen: lighted splint, squeaky pop.
Oxygen: glowing splint relights.
Carbon dioxide: limewater turns milky.
Chloride: nitric acid then silver nitrate, white precipitate.
Sulfate: hydrochloric acid then barium chloride, white precipitate.

panels.title: Safety
points: Eye protection for all practicals.
Heat crystallising solutions gently; do not boil dry.
Handle hot crucibles with tongs.
Acids and alkalis are irritants: wash spills with water.
